approachQuestion.prompt: The input sequence is exactly [1,2,...,n] and target is a permutation of those distinct values; n may be zero and is at most 100,000. Starting with an empty stack, you may push the next input value or pop the top. Can the complete target be emitted? Return one boolean. Example target [2,1,4,3] -> true; [3,1,2] -> false.

options.text: Simulate pushes in order; after each push, pop while the stack top equals the next target value. Accept iff all target values are emitted.
options.feedback: For target [3,1,2], after emitting 3 the stack contains 1,2; 1 cannot be popped next.

options.text: For each target prefix, restart a simulation from the beginning to decide if it can be emitted.
options.feedback: Restarting simulation preserves the exact operation rules, but redoes prior pushes for each target element.

options.text: Compare input and target positions directly.
options.feedback: [2,1,4,3] is valid despite differing positions; direct comparison rejects it.

options.text: Enumerate every possible sequence of legal stack operations and keep the one that produces the requested result.
options.feedback: The number of operation sequences grows exponentially; simulating the forced next output avoids exploring irrelevant choices.

details: Simulate pushes in order; after each push, pop while the stack top equals the next target value. Accept iff all target values are emitted.

Pop greedily whenever the top matches the next target: delaying that available pop cannot expose a deeper required value sooner. If the next target stays buried after all pushes, the permutation is impossible.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For stack-permutation-validation-optimal, let n be the number of input commands or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Input is immutable; output storage is excluded.
constraints: Every stack push/pop and fixed-size operation takes constant time. The implementation is iterative; call-stack space is O(1).
The input may force a stack containing a linear number of entries. No hidden copying of the entire input occurs.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each input value is pushed once and popped at most once.
details: Each value is pushed once and popped at most once during the target simulation. Target [n,n-1,...,1] retains n values before the first pop, attaining linear auxiliary space.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The target [n,n-1,...,1] requires pushing all n values before the first pop, attaining n working entries.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Every input value is pushed once and popped at most once during the entire target simulation.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A late impossible target position can require processing the preceding permutation before rejection.
